author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyA New Fossil Hints at the Surprising Origins of SnakesBy the Cretaceous, they’d already tried on several different lifestyles and sensory stylesDRBy Devin Reese12:00 PM CDT on October 22, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleBiologists have long debated snake origins. Did they evolve in the sea, underground, or on land, given that today they inhabit all those environments? Now, an exceptionally preserved Cretaceous fossil found in 2020 west of São Paulo, Brazil, sheds a bit of light on snake origins.A study recently published in the journal Nature described the fossil of a newly identified, very early snake ancestor species, Tametara mirim gen. et sp. nov., that was about the length of the bottom of a coat hanger. Based on its skull anatomy, the authors suggested that the snake led a burrowing lifestyle. Read more: “Snakes Break All the Rules”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
